//: Which drawing in which source file is which species. `group` is the index of a top-level <g> in the file - run `npm run animal-art -- --index` to print a labelled contact sheet and read the numbers off it. `flip` mirrors a drawing so every animal in the game faces the same way (right).

sources.//: No usable groups on this sheet, so the birds are found as islands. `drop` removes the sheet's own teal shadow puddle, which would otherwise sit on the grass. `unitScale` puts this sheet's units on the same scale as the first one: not by biology - the sheet draws small animals two to four times life size, so a flamingo sized truthfully looks shrunken beside an inflated fox. It is set to sit where the sheet would have drawn it.

A jungle scene: every animal sits among the same foliage, so islands weld them together and each is named by the patch it occupies instead. The parrot stands alone and comes out as an island. No gorilla here - the apes on this sheet are chimpanzees, and labelling one a gorilla would be a lie the game repeats to a room full of people.

Each animal sits on a pale blob the colour of the sheet's own backdrop, so that colour is dropped. The gorilla is taken by region rather than as an island: its body alone is a fifth of the page, and the island finder treats anything that big as scenery.
Drawn three-quarter on rather than in profile like the other sheets, so only taken where the pose earns it. A sitting panda reads as a sitting panda from any angle.
